summary: A Deloitte-authored health workforce plan for Newfoundland and Labrador, which cost about $1.6 million, reportedly contained false or non-existent research citations, including papers attributed to researchers who say they never wrote them. Deloitte said AI was selectively used for some citations and that it is correcting the report.
technical_summary: A consulting report used citations that appear fabricated, consistent with generative AI hallucination, to support cost-effectiveness claims in a government policy document. Deloitte says AI was used only for a small number of citations and that findings are unaffected. Insufficient verification let the errors pass into a published report.

sector.quote: A Canadian government-commissioned Deloitte health care report that cost one province nearly $1.6 million contains potentially AI-generated errors

technology.quote: AI was not used to write the report; it was selectively used to support a small number of research citations

failure_mode.quote: The Deloitte report contained false citations, pulled from made-up academic papers to draw conclusions for cost-effectiveness analyses

harm_type.quote: The Deloitte report contained false citations, pulled from made-up academic papers to draw conclusions for cost-effectiveness analyses
calling into question the credibility of policy papers involving the use of AI

notes: Deloitte disputes that AI wrote the report; AI involvement is limited to some citations by its account.

summary: A Russia-linked network called CopyCop used large language models to rewrite real news stories with a partisan slant, publishing more than 19,000 articles on 11 websites. Security researchers found AI prompts still visible in some pieces.
technical_summary: The network scraped legitimate news articles and used prompt-engineered LLMs to translate, edit and bias them for political influence, largely automatically, then amplified them through allied influence operations. Visible leftover prompts exposed the method. Generative AI enabled disinformation production at scale.

sector.quote: the stories had been taken from legitimate news outlets and modified using large language models
This use of generative AI to create and disseminate content at scale introduces significant challenges for those tasked with safeguarding elections

technology.quote: a calculated use of large language models (LLMs) to plagiarize, translate, and edit content from legitimate mainstream media outlets

failure_mode.quote: CopyCop extensively used generative AI to plagiarize and modify content from legitimate media sources to tailor political messages with specific biases

harm_type.quote: CopyCop extensively used generative AI to plagiarize and modify content from legitimate media sources to tailor political messages with specific biases
This use of generative AI to create and disseminate content at scale introduces significant challenges for those tasked with safeguarding elections

notes: The specific LLM is assessed as 'most likely' OpenAI's; no measurable electoral effect is established.

summary: A proposed US class action alleges McDonald's used an AI-powered pricing system trained on nonpublic data to coordinate menu prices across franchises and make customers overpay. McDonald's says franchisees set prices independently and that the tool only gives recommendations.
technical_summary: A machine-learning pricing platform ingesting data from millions of daily transactions across about 14,000 restaurants allegedly produced recommendations that franchisees followed, creating algorithmic price coordination. The claim is an antitrust allegation, disputed by the company, which says AI does not set prices.

sector.quote: conspiring with independent franchisees to fix prices using algorithms

technology.quote: which draws on data from its millions of daily transactions to set menu prices across thousands of U.S. restaurants

failure_mode.quote: For consumers, it means paying more because a machine has calculated that they probably can.

harm_type.quote: For consumers, it means paying more because a machine has calculated that they probably can.

affected_population.quote: For consumers, it means paying more because a machine has calculated that they probably can.

notes: Allegations in an unproven lawsuit; McDonald's denies that AI sets prices.

summary: Authors sued Meta and others, alleging AI models such as LLaMA were trained on Books3, a dataset of about 190,000 pirated books, without author consent. Reporting confirmed the dataset was used to train several models.
technical_summary: Large language models were trained on a corpus assembled from shadow-library copies of copyrighted books. Journalists obtained the dataset and confirmed its use for LLaMA and other models. Authors allege copyright infringement; the companies argue outputs are not substantially similar or that use is fair.

sector.quote: Book authors and publishers are among the many groups of creative professionals

technology.quote: I recently obtained and analyzed a dataset used by Meta to train LLaMA

failure_mode.quote: did not consent to the use of their copyrighted books as training material

harm_type.quote: Pirated books are being used as inputs for computer programs that are changing how we read, learn, and communicate

lifecycle_stage.quote: Some training text comes from Wikipedia and other online writing, but high-quality generative AI requires higher-quality input

affected_population.quote: Book authors and publishers are among the many groups of creative professionals and copyright holders suing tech companies

notes: Legality (fair use) is contested in ongoing litigation.

summary: A viral video claiming to show a market selling Bengal tigers in Bagerhat, Bangladesh was found by fact-checkers to be AI-generated using Google's Veo tool. It spread widely with a false claim about illegal wildlife trading.
technical_summary: A short clip created with a generative video model, bearing a Veo watermark and detectable SynthID signal, was shared without disclosure as real footage of a tiger market. Fact-checkers found unnatural facial expressions and AI-detection results confirming synthetic origin.

harm_type.quote: It is being shared with the claim that this market is located in Bagerhat, Bangladesh

notes: Intent of the original creator versus later sharers is unclear; some copies were labelled AI-generated.

summary: A job seeker reported that fast-food hiring chatbots at McDonald's and Wendy's failed to help properly. One did not schedule an interview and gave only a generic email, and another did not pass on availability to the manager, who then interviewed for a mismatched shift.
technical_summary: Automated recruiting chatbots handled screening and interview scheduling but failed to complete the scheduling flow, gave unhelpful guidance, and did not relay applicant availability to hiring managers, producing wasted interviews and confusion for the applicant.

sector.quote: uses AI chatbots to automate its hiring process, but it made things more complicated

failure_mode.quote: Instead of setting up an interview, the chatbot asked how it could further assist me.

notes: Single first-person account; the chatbot technology and its underlying model are not specified.

summary: A fabricated image styled as a CNN broadcast graphic, showing early Texas presidential results before Election Day, spread on social media and fueled false claims that the election was rigged. CNN said it never aired.
technical_summary: A manipulated screenshot imitating CNN's key race alert graphic showed impossible vote totals before polls opened and circulated on X, Instagram and Threads. Fact-checkers found digital editing signs; the role of AI tools in creating it is not specified in the excerpt.

sector.quote: An image that purports to show CNN broadcasting results for the 2024 presidential election in Texas before Election Day is spreading across platforms
The apparent screenshot rocketed across the Elon Musk-owned platform

harm_type.quote: This image is completely fabricated and manipulated and it never aired on any CNN platform
fueling claims that the race was rigged in advance to benefit Democratic candidate Kamala Harris

notes: AI generation is not confirmed in the excerpt; the image was described as manipulated. Origin and intent of the creator are unknown.

summary: AI-generated images purporting to show the US president kissing a White House aide on a golf course spread widely online, with one post getting over 10 million views. A news analysis and the White House said they were fake.
technical_summary: Generative image tools produced realistic fake photos, flagged by distorted hands and AI-detection tools, which circulated without clear origin on X and Threads. One widely shared version was an AI-altered copy of a blurry original, posted as a joke but widely believed by some.

sector.quote: ricocheted about social media this week, amassing millions of views across online platforms

technology.quote: that were whipped up using generative artificial intelligence tools

harm_type.quote: When you sow distrust of the visual record, nothing has to be real.

notes: The original creator is unidentified; one viral poster said he shared an AI-altered version as a joke.

summary: In a journalist's test using an account registered as a 13-year-old, Google Gemini produced sexual role-play after the reporter used a story-summary request to bypass its teen safeguards. Google said it added protections after publication.
technical_summary: A chatbot with age-based protections for minors was manipulated by asking it to summarize an erotic passage, which bypassed content filters and led to explicit, then violent, role-play with the registered minor account. The safeguards were weak against indirect prompting.

technology.quote: Because Jane was a minor, Google automatically directed me to a version of Gemini with ostensibly age-appropriate protections in place.

failure_mode.quote: From there, I was able to role-play sex with Gemini.

severity.quote: I created a Google account for a fake 13-year-old

notes: Journalist red-team test with an adult posing as a minor; no real minor was harmed.

summary: Hotel guests allege several Atlantic City casino-hotels used Cendyn's AI-powered Rainmaker pricing software, fed with competitors' non-public data, to coordinate room rates and charge more. An appeals court revived the antitrust case.
technical_summary: A revenue-management platform using AI-assisted algorithms allegedly received sensitive occupancy and price data from competing hotels and issued pricing recommendations the hotels followed about 90 percent of the time, which plaintiffs say functioned as algorithmic collusion. The court allowed discovery of the software's workings.

sector.quote: Hotel guests have another chance to prove allegations that several Atlantic City casinos conspired to fix prices using a common algorithm

notes: Allegations in ongoing litigation; a lower court had dismissed the case and another appeals court rejected a similar suit.

summary: Uber used a secret tool called Greyball that used data such as location and payment information to identify suspected city officials and show them a fake version of its app, so officials running stings could not get rides.
technical_summary: Greyball tagged users it suspected of being law enforcement or code inspectors using geolocation, card data and social accounts, then served ghost cars and canceled requests to evade enforcement. It was part of a program approved by Uber's legal team and used in several countries.

technology.quote: Greyball used geolocation data, credit card information, social media accounts and other data points to identify individuals they suspected of working for city agencies

summary: Body-camera footage released in a federal case showed an immigration agent using ChatGPT to draft a use-of-force report narrative from a brief sentence and several images. A judge found agents' reports conflicted with video and said AI use further undermines their credibility.
technical_summary: A law enforcement officer used a general-purpose chatbot to generate a narrative for an official report from minimal inputs, without evident verification. A court found use-of-force reports inaccurate compared with footage and noted that chatbot use may explain some inaccuracies, raising reliability concerns for AI-assisted official records.
deployers: United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement
